To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) cancer cells have a high energy demand that is met by a metabolic shift towards glycolysis and glutaminolysis, 2) the high energy demand is sustained by a specific set of intracellular messangers, such as calcium, that are involved in the regulation of the metabolic shift and 3) the metabolic shift is regulated by specific factors that are expressed in cancer stem cells and are overactivated by the tumor microenvironment
cancer is a disease of the mitochondrion and that the tumor microenvironment (TME) is a crucial player in the control of the tumor cell phenotype.

the TME is the main driver of cancer progression and that the TME should be considered as the ‘fourth dimension of cancer’ (in addition to the three dimensions of space and the fourth dimension of time) [4].
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular and cellular mechanisms of cancer development and progression.
the identification of novel targets for anticancer therapy, and with the identification of new strategies for the development of novel anticancer drugs.
the identification of the mechanisms that underlie the development of cancer and the design of novel therapeutic strategies to counteract the disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cancer research has entered an era of unprecedented acceleration and effectiveness, and that the future of cancer treatment is bright.
the last few years have seen the emergence of a novel ‘ecosystem’ of cancer research that has allowed to identify new and promising targets, and to develop innovative anticancer strategies.
cancer research is currently undergoing a renaissance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cancer field has witnessed a rapid accumulation of basic and clinically relevant information that will allow us to better understand the molecular basis of cancer and to design novel effective anticancer strategies.
we have entered the era of personalized therapy for cancer.
we have moved from a ‘cell-centric’ to a ‘cell-ecology’ view of cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TME has the capacity to modulate cancer cell metabolism and, as a result, the response to therapy, thus opening the possibility of developing novel anticancer strategies.

the cancer cell has a unique metabolic signature, that is, a metabolic fingerprint, and that this signature can be used to identify cancer cells and, more importantly, to discriminate between cancer cells that are sensitive or resistant to specific drugs or treatments.
cancer is not only a disease of the cells but also a disease of the tissues and the microenvironment in which the cells live.
